title: Treasury Sanctions Recruitment Network Enabling War in Sudan, Calls for Humanitarian Truce
summary: The U.S. Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) imposed sanctions on five individuals and entities involved in recruiting former Colombian military personnel to fight for the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) in Sudan's civil war, marking the third anniversary of the conflict. The sanctions target employment agencies and recruiters operating primarily from Colombia, including International Services Agency (A4SI), its successor Fénix Human Resources S.A.S., and associated individuals. The Trump Administration is calling for an immediate three-month humanitarian truce without preconditions.
key_points: OFAC designated five individuals and entities under Executive Order 14098 for their roles in recruiting foreign fighters for the RSF in Sudan
The sanctions target a network including Alvaro Andres Quijano Becerra, his wife Claudia Viviana Oliveros Forero, and their Colombia-based employment agency A4SI
Fénix Human Resources S.A.S. was opened in February 2025 as a replacement for A4SI
Jose Libardo Quijano Torres is the nominal manager of Fénix; Omar Fernando Garcia Batte is Fénix's legal representative
Jose Oscar Garcia Batte, through Global Qowa Al-Basheria S.A.S. (GQAB), recruited individuals who did not meet fitness requirements and continued recruiting after learning fighters were sent to Sudan
The conflict has killed over 150,000 people, displaced more than 14 million, and created famine conditions since April 2023
